notes:
=== INITIAL ENUMERATION METHODOLOGY ===
Run immediately after landing a foothold, before any exploitation attempt.

COMMAND SEQUENCE AND PURPOSE:
tasklist /svc          → maps running processes to their service names
set                    → dumps all environment variables (PATH leaks, temp dirs, credentials)
systeminfo             → OS version, patch level, architecture, domain membership
wmic qfe list brief    → installed hotfixes with date — cross-ref with Watson/WES-NG
netstat -ano           → active connections + listening ports (find locally-bound services)
whoami /priv           → privilege token — first stop for escalation path selection
whoami /groups         → group membership including implicit groups (NETWORK SERVICE, etc.)
net user               → local account list
net localgroup         → local group membership
net localgroup administrators → confirm admin group members

=== ACCESS TOKENS ===
Every process carries a primary token. Services impersonate via impersonation tokens.
SeImpersonatePrivilege on a service account = Potato attack available.
Disabled privileges in whoami /priv are still assigned — they can be enabled with scripts.
Non-elevated admin sessions have privileges stripped by UAC — elevated session shows full set.

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
systeminfo → Watson → kernel exploit path
whoami /priv → SeImpersonate → JuicyPotato/PrintSpoofer
whoami /groups → Backup Operators → NTDS.dit extraction
netstat -ano → locally bound service → Druva-style RPC exploitation
net localgroup → Event Log Readers → Security log credential harvest

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
Any privilege beyond SeChangeNotifyPrivilege on a standard account
Group memberships: Backup Operators, Print Operators, Server Operators, DnsAdmins, Event Log Readers
Domain-joined vs workgroup — affects which AD escalation paths apply
OS version + missing KBs → HiveNightmare (Win10), PrintNightmare (pre-patch), EternalBlue

recommended.note: Check your privileges and group memberships next.
Map missing patches to kernel exploits.

name: WinPE - Initial System Enumeration
description: Baseline host enumeration: OS/patch level, running processes and services, installed software, hotfixes, and listening ports. Feeds patch/service-based escalation paths.

variations.label: System / patches
variations.command:
systeminfo
wmic qfe
Get-HotFix | ft -AutoSize
set

variations.label: Processes / services
variations.command:
tasklist /svc
sc query
wmic product get name
Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product | select Name,Version

variations.label: CimInstance services
variations.command:
Get-CimInstance -ClassName win32_service | Select Name,State,PathName | Where-Object {$_.State -like 'Running'}
Get-CimInstance win32_service | Where-Object {$_.StartName -notmatch 'LocalSystem|LocalService|NetworkService'} | Select Name,StartName,PathName

variations.label: CimInstance patches
variations.command: Get-CimInstance -Class win32_quickfixengineering | Where-Object { $_.Description -eq 'Security Update' } | Select HotFixID,InstalledOn | Sort InstalledOn
